text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY

- Rem Vyakhirev, head of Russia's giant natural gas monopoly Gazprom, gave an upbeat assessment of his company's future at a government meeting on Thursday, promising to reduce wholesale prices and hive off unwieldy non-core businesses.
- A Russian-Finnish-German consortium has announced plans to build in Russia Adam Opel's latest Astra car model.
- First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais says Russia will sign a trade agreement with De Beers diamond firm in June.
- The government agrees on the basic course of change for the gas monopoly Gazprom set out by its chairman Vyakhirev.
- Tax authorities propose introducing a new tax on veksel promissory notes.
- Kazakhstan tightens border controls with CIS countries.
- Two tin-can producing plants will be built near Moscow shortly. Their joint capacity will exceed prospective demand by 50 percent.
- The Central Bank will exert firmer control over multiple branch commercial banks.
- The government will lend a helping hand to Gazprom in its attempts to keep foreign speculators off its shares.
SEVODNYA
- The government will have to consider cutting some social benefit programmes.
- Gazprom will not let fresh-faced reformers in the cabinet take control of its reform programme.
- Chubais says Yakutia has a formidable potential for development.
- Moscow city expects it will receive a $100,000 syndicated loan at a very low interest rate from a group of foreign banks in June.
- The latest basic specification Volkswagen Passat saloon car will cost $23,000 in Moscow.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The fate of Gazprom is in the hands of Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
- The Duma is unlikely to vote for the budget cuts proposed by the government.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- Gazprom will cut 100,000 jobs in a proposed restructuring programme.
- Experts give high marks to all latest decrees by President Yeltsin.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais has moved to assert control over Russian diamond-mining industry.

- An undercover fight for control over Russian industrial and financial resources continues and First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov could soon become a key figure in the tug of war between different groups.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
